title.narrative: ADR entrenched as a mechanism for resolving legal disputes and human rights complaints

description.narrative: Article 252 of the Constitution of Kenya as read with the KNCHR Act empowers the Commission to employ alternative methods of dispute resolution including mediation, negotiation and conciliation. Through the project, the commission applies and promoted the use of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) by other actors.

description.narrative: The number of cases admitted by KNCHR which were handled through alternative dispute resolution mechanism.

comment.narrative: Six (6) cases handled through ADR. They were on Land and property rights and Healthcare issues

title.narrative: Systemic human rights violations resolved through Public Interest Litigation (PIL)

description.narrative: Public Interest Litigation (PIL) is one of the means by which the Commission is able to influence policy direction and interpretation of the Constitution through the judicial process. It also serves as a mechanism for the resolving human rights violations. The Commission participates in PIL through either originating petitions in its own name or joining existing petitions filed by other parties which have a major public interest component either as amicus curiae or an interested party as appropriate.

title.narrative: Improved access to and timely processing of human rights complaints, with particular attention to SGBV cases

description.narrative: The KNCHR in line with its statutory and constitutional mandate receive and process complaints on alleged human rights violations. Complaints that fall within the KNCHR’s mandate are subjected to further analysis and follow up that includes among others investigations. Complaints that fall outside the KNCHR’s mandate are referred to relevant complaints handling institutions for further action.

title.narrative: No. of investigations and recommendations documented

description.narrative: The total number of investigations conducted with investigation reports highlighting recommendations to various target groups.

comment.narrative: A total of Twenty-two (22) investigation missions were conducted for 19 cases. These included cases of suspected abductions, ethnic conflict-related violence, violations of land and labor rights, and the obstruction of access to education and justice. Reports also highlighted claims of torture, extrajudicial killings, sexual exploitation, and the excessive use of force by security agencies and conservancy personnel. Additionally, inquiries were launched into incidents affecting vulnerable communities and detainees, as well as the disruption of public services such as education and worship. These efforts reflect an ongoing commitment to addressing systemic injustices and safeguarding human rights nationwide.

title.narrative: No. of audits done in the tea sector to address SGBV/reports developed
A victim-cantered human rights based approach (HRBA) integrated in the delivery of justice.

description.narrative: This objective will aim to intensify the advocacy for Human Rights Based Approach (HRBA) in delivery of justice. In doing so, the National Commission is to adopt the following approaches: Capacity building of justice actors; trial observations & targeted court observations; strengthening the legal capacity for persons with disabilities and advocacy for establishment and actualization of reparations mechanism.

title.narrative: No. of justice sector forums (CUC forums) hosted

comment.narrative: Two (2) forums with CUCs from Voi and Rongo Law Courts. The CUCs from Rongo were trained and sensitised on multi-sectoral approach in handling and management of SGBV cases. In Voi, discussions focused on mental health challenges requiring psychiatric services, logistics for the Voi Small Claims Court, resource constraints faced by the Department of Child Services (DCS), and establishment of a children's remand center. Challenges identified included lack of funding, understaffing, absence of mobility resources for DCS, and inactivity of the Wildlife Claims Committee, hindering resolution of human-wildlife conflicts. An Integrity Sub-Committee chaired by the presiding judge was established to tackle corruption.In addition, one (1) community outreach was conducted to discuss the rise of insecurity cases in kisauni mtopanga ward and its impact on human rights. As a result, a total of 22 participants (12 females and 10 males) were engaged in a bid to address security concerns and discuss human rights, child rights, bail and bond, and community-led crime prevention strategies.

title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity for project implementation

description.narrative: Through the project, the commission will ensure efficient and effective utilization of resources, accountability, effective monitoring and evaluation of the entire process. The National Commission will also work towards strengthening its Human Resources; leveraging on Information and Communication Technology (ICT), strengthen internal policies, systems and processes for effective service delivery.
